functions.name: amqp_version_number
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT uint32_t AMQP_CALL amqp_version_number(void);
functions.description: Returns the rabbitmq-c library version as a packed 32-bit integer per AMQP_VERSION format. Use to compare runtime library version to compile-time macros.
requirements: No arguments.
Return is a packed 32-bit value; compare using AMQP_VERSION_CODE or documented bit layout.

functions.name: amqp_version
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT char const *AMQP_CALL amqp_version(void);
functions.description: Returns a statically allocated, null-terminated string describing the library version (may include "-pre" for non-releases).
requirements: Returned pointer is statically allocated; do not free or modify.
String remains valid for process lifetime.

functions.name: init_amqp_pool
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT void AMQP_CALL init_amqp_pool(amqp_pool_t *pool, size_t pagesize);
functions.description: Initializes an amqp_pool_t memory pool with the given page size so it can service allocations.
requirements: pool must point to an amqp_pool_t structure.
Must be called exactly once before using the pool; calling on an already-initialized pool results in undefined behavior.
pagesize determines allocation granularity; allocations > pagesize will be placed in large_blocks.

functions.name: recycle_amqp_pool
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT void AMQP_CALL recycle_amqp_pool(amqp_pool_t *pool);
functions.description: Recycles memory within the pool for reuse without necessarily returning memory to the system. All previous allocations from the pool become invalid.
requirements: pool must be an initialized amqp_pool_t.
After calling, any memory previously returned from this pool must no longer be used.

functions.name: empty_amqp_pool
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT void AMQP_CALL empty_amqp_pool(amqp_pool_t *pool);
functions.description: Releases all memory associated with the pool, effectively emptying it.
requirements: pool must be an initialized amqp_pool_t.
All allocations from the pool become invalid after this call.

functions.name: amqp_pool_alloc
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT void *AMQP_CALL amqp_pool_alloc(amqp_pool_t *pool, size_t amount);
functions.description: Allocates a block of memory from the pool. Allocations are 8-byte aligned. Returns NULL if amount is 0 or if allocation fails.
requirements: pool must be initialized via init_amqp_pool.
amount may be 0 (returns NULL).
Returned memory is owned by the pool; it becomes invalid after recycle_amqp_pool() or empty_amqp_pool().
Do not free with free(); managed by the pool.

functions.name: amqp_pool_alloc_bytes
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT void AMQP_CALL amqp_pool_alloc_bytes(amqp_pool_t *pool, size_t amount, amqp_bytes_t *output);
functions.description: Allocates a buffer from the pool and returns it as amqp_bytes_t with 8-byte alignment. On error or zero length, sets output.bytes=NULL and output.len=0.
requirements: pool must be initialized.
output must be a valid pointer to amqp_bytes_t.
amount may be 0 (output becomes empty).
Memory is owned by the pool and invalidated by recycle/empty of the pool; do not free with free().

functions.name: amqp_cstring_bytes
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_bytes_t AMQP_CALL amqp_cstring_bytes(char const *cstr);
functions.description: Wraps a C string (null-terminated) in an amqp_bytes_t without copying.
requirements: cstr must be a valid null-terminated string; function uses strlen().
Returned amqp_bytes_t points to the original buffer; caller must ensure it remains valid for the period of use.
Do not modify through this wrapper unless underlying string is mutable and owned by caller.

functions.name: amqp_bytes_malloc_dup
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_bytes_t AMQP_CALL amqp_bytes_malloc_dup(amqp_bytes_t src);
functions.description: Allocates and duplicates the contents of src into a new amqp_bytes_t buffer allocated by amqp_bytes_malloc().
requirements: On success, free the returned buffer with amqp_bytes_free().
If allocation fails, returned .bytes will be NULL and .len may be 0.

functions.name: amqp_bytes_malloc
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_bytes_t AMQP_CALL amqp_bytes_malloc(size_t amount);
functions.description: Allocates a new amqp_bytes_t buffer of the requested size. On failure, .bytes is NULL.
requirements: On success, release with amqp_bytes_free().
amount specifies size in bytes; if allocation fails, .bytes == NULL (check before use).

functions.name: amqp_bytes_free
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT void AMQP_CALL amqp_bytes_free(amqp_bytes_t bytes);
functions.description: Frees a buffer previously allocated by amqp_bytes_malloc() or amqp_bytes_malloc_dup().
requirements: bytes must have been allocated by amqp_bytes_malloc() or amqp_bytes_malloc_dup(); freeing other buffers is undefined behavior.
After call, the memory is invalid.

functions.name: amqp_new_connection
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_connection_state_t AMQP_CALL amqp_new_connection(void);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes a new AMQP connection state object. Must later be destroyed with amqp_destroy_connection().
requirements: Returns NULL on failure; check before use.
Destroy with amqp_destroy_connection() to free resources.

functions.name: amqp_get_sockfd
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_get_sockfd(amqp_connection_state_t state);
functions.description: Returns the underlying socket descriptor associated with the connection, or -1 if none is set. Use with caution as manipulating the socket externally can cause undefined behavior.
requirements: state must be a valid connection state.
Caller must not perform operations on the socket that interfere with rabbitmq-c’s expectations.

functions.name: amqp_set_sockfd
functions.signature: AMQP_DEPRECATED_EXPORT void AMQP_CALL amqp_set_sockfd(amqp_connection_state_t state, int sockfd);
functions.description: Deprecated: Associates an existing connected socket descriptor with the connection. Prefer amqp_tcp_socket_new()/amqp_ssl_socket_new() and amqp_set_socket().
requirements: state must be valid.
sockfd must be a connected socket and must not be used for I/O by the caller before handing to the library.
Using deprecated API; behavior may change and is discouraged.

functions.name: amqp_tune_connection
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_tune_connection(amqp_connection_state_t state, int channel_max, int frame_max, int heartbeat);
functions.description: Adjusts client-side channel_max, frame_max, and heartbeat values without renegotiation with the broker. Intended for internal/library use; may abort() in some states.
requirements: state must be valid.
channel_max must be between 0 and 65535 (doc notes maximum 65535).
frame_max must be >= 4096 and <= 2147483647; 131072 recommended unless you know what you’re doing.
heartbeat is number of seconds between heartbeats (>= 0).
May return AMQP_STATUS_NO_MEMORY or AMQP_STATUS_TIMER_FAILURE; caller must handle non-OK results.
Do not call from external code unless you understand implications; may call abort().

functions.name: amqp_get_channel_max
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_get_channel_max(amqp_connection_state_t state);
functions.description: Returns the negotiated maximum number of channels for the connection (0 means no limit).
requirements: state must be valid.
Negotiated during amqp_login()/amqp_login_with_properties().

functions.name: amqp_get_frame_max
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_get_frame_max(amqp_connection_state_t state);
functions.description: Returns the negotiated maximum AMQP frame size in bytes for the connection.
requirements: state must be valid.
Negotiated during amqp_login()/amqp_login_with_properties().

functions.name: amqp_get_heartbeat
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_get_heartbeat(amqp_connection_state_t state);
functions.description: Returns the negotiated heartbeat interval in seconds for the connection.
requirements: state must be valid.
Negotiated during amqp_login()/amqp_login_with_properties().

functions.name: amqp_destroy_connection
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_destroy_connection(amqp_connection_state_t state);
functions.description: Destroys a connection state object. If connected, implicitly closes the connection (reply code 200), frees internal buffers, and invalidates memory that may be released by maybe_release_buffers functions.
requirements: state must be a connection created by amqp_new_connection().
After calling, state must not be used.
Returns AMQP_STATUS_OK on success; handle non-OK values.

functions.name: amqp_handle_input
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_handle_input(amqp_connection_state_t state, amqp_bytes_t received_data, amqp_frame_t *decoded_frame);
functions.description: Low-level processing of incoming bytes: decodes the first complete AMQP frame from the provided buffer and reports how many bytes were consumed. decoded_frame may contain pointers into connection-owned memory.
requirements: state must be valid.
received_data.bytes/.len must refer to received bytes; function copies consumed bytes internally.
decoded_frame must be a valid pointer to amqp_frame_t; on success frame_type != 0 indicates a frame decoded.
Caller must adjust its buffer by the returned byte count to process remaining data.
On error, negative amqp_status_enum is returned; caller should handle conditions including BAD_AMQP_DATA, UNKNOWN_METHOD/CLASS, NO_MEMORY, etc.
Any memory referenced by decoded_frame is owned by the connection and may be invalidated by amqp_maybe_release_buffers[_on_channel]().

functions.name: amqp_release_buffers_ok
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_boolean_t AMQP_CALL amqp_release_buffers_ok(amqp_connection_state_t state);
functions.description: Deprecated: Checks whether it is currently safe to call amqp_release_buffers() on the connection.
requirements: state must be valid.
If returns true, caller may call amqp_release_buffers(); otherwise do not call.

functions.name: amqp_release_buffers
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT void AMQP_CALL amqp_release_buffers(amqp_connection_state_t state);
functions.description: Deprecated: Releases connection-owned buffers for reuse by the library. May abort() if called when amqp_release_buffers_ok() is false. Any previously returned memory becomes invalid.
requirements: state must be valid.
Caller should ensure amqp_release_buffers_ok(state) returns true before calling to avoid abort().
After calling, do not use memory previously returned by the library.

functions.name: amqp_maybe_release_buffers
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT void AMQP_CALL amqp_maybe_release_buffers(amqp_connection_state_t state);
functions.description: Releases connection-owned buffers related to any channel when safe to do so, allowing memory reuse by the library.
requirements: state must be valid.
Any memory previously returned by the library for any channel becomes invalid after this call.

functions.name: amqp_maybe_release_buffers_on_channel
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT void AMQP_CALL amqp_maybe_release_buffers_on_channel(amqp_connection_state_t state, amqp_channel_t channel);
functions.description: Releases connection-owned buffers associated with the specified channel when safe to do so, allowing memory reuse.
requirements: state must be valid.
channel is the channel whose buffers may be released; library does not require a particular channel state.
Memory previously returned by the library for this channel becomes invalid after this call.

functions.name: amqp_send_frame
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_send_frame(amqp_connection_state_t state, amqp_frame_t const *frame);
functions.description: Serializes and sends an AMQP frame to the broker. Returns AMQP_STATUS_OK on success or a negative amqp_status_enum on error.
requirements: state must be a connected connection with an assigned/open socket.
frame must point to a properly formed frame matching its frame_type.
Caller must handle possible errors including BAD_AMQP_DATA, TABLE_TOO_BIG, UNKNOWN_METHOD/CLASS, TIMER_FAILURE, SOCKET_ERROR, SSL_ERROR.

functions.name: amqp_table_entry_cmp
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_table_entry_cmp(void const *entry1, void const *entry2);
functions.description: Compares two amqp_table_entry_t entries (by key, type, then value) like strcmp().
requirements: entry1 and entry2 must point to amqp_table_entry_t objects.
Returns 0 if equal, <0 if left<right, >0 if left>right.

functions.name: amqp_open_socket
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_open_socket(char const *hostname, int portnumber);
functions.description: Deprecated low-level helper: resolves hostname and opens a TCP socket to the given host:port, setting socket options. Returns socket fd on success or negative amqp_status_enum on error.
requirements: hostname must be a valid host or IP (IPv4/IPv6).
portnumber must be a valid port.
Caller is responsible for closing the returned socket and integrating with connection APIs.
Errors include AMQP_STATUS_TCP_SOCKETLIB_INIT_ERROR, HOSTNAME_RESOLUTION_FAILED, SOCKET_ERROR.

functions.name: amqp_send_header
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_send_header(amqp_connection_state_t state);
functions.description: Sends the initial AMQP protocol header to the broker on the connection.
requirements: state must be valid and have an open/connected socket.
On failure, returns negative amqp_status_enum (e.g., CONNECTION_CLOSED, SOCKET_ERROR, SSL_ERROR). Caller must handle errors.

functions.name: amqp_frames_enqueued
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_boolean_t AMQP_CALL amqp_frames_enqueued(amqp_connection_state_t state);
functions.description: Checks whether the connection has buffered AMQP frames ready to be read without blocking.
requirements: state must be valid.
TRUE means amqp_simple_wait_frame[_noblock] can return immediately.

functions.name: amqp_simple_wait_frame
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_simple_wait_frame(amqp_connection_state_t state, amqp_frame_t *decoded_frame);
functions.description: Waits (potentially blocking) for the next frame from the broker and decodes it into decoded_frame. May return immediately if frames are buffered or data already in read buffer.
requirements: state must be valid and connected.
decoded_frame must be a valid pointer.
Caller must handle negative amqp_status_enum errors (NO_MEMORY, BAD_AMQP_DATA, UNKNOWN_METHOD/CLASS, HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT, TIMER_FAILURE, SOCKET_ERROR, SSL_ERROR).
This function does not return heartbeat frames as of v0.4.0 (handled internally).

functions.name: amqp_simple_wait_frame_noblock
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_simple_wait_frame_noblock(amqp_connection_state_t state, amqp_frame_t *decoded_frame, const struct timeval *tv);
functions.description: Waits up to the specified timeout for a frame and decodes it. With tv==NULL behaves like blocking amqp_simple_wait_frame; with {0,0} behaves non-blocking. Returns AMQP_STATUS_TIMEOUT on timeout.
requirements: state must be valid and connected.
decoded_frame must be a valid pointer.
tv may be NULL (block), or a valid pointer to struct timeval; invalid values yield AMQP_STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER.
Caller must handle errors listed in docs, including TIMEOUT.

functions.name: amqp_simple_wait_method
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_simple_wait_method(amqp_connection_state_t state, amqp_channel_t expected_channel, amqp_method_number_t expected_method, amqp_method_t *output);
functions.description: Waits for a single specific method frame on a given channel and returns it in output. Warning: will close the connection on unexpected frames per documented behavior.
requirements: state must be valid and connected.
output must be a valid pointer.
expected_channel and expected_method specify required frame; wrong method/channel/frame type may yield AMQP_STATUS_WRONG_METHOD and close the connection.
Caller must handle other negative amqp_status_enum values.

functions.name: amqp_send_method
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_send_method(amqp_connection_state_t state, amqp_channel_t channel, amqp_method_number_t id, void *decoded);
functions.description: Convenience wrapper to send a method frame with the given method id and decoded method payload on a channel.
requirements: state must be valid and connected.
decoded must point to the appropriate decoded method struct for id.
Caller must handle possible amqp_status_enum errors (BAD_AMQP_DATA, TABLE_TOO_BIG, UNKNOWN_METHOD/CLASS, TIMER_FAILURE, SOCKET/SSL errors).

functions.name: amqp_simple_rpc
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_rpc_reply_t AMQP_CALL amqp_simple_rpc(amqp_connection_state_t state, amqp_channel_t channel, amqp_method_number_t request_id, amqp_method_number_t *expected_reply_ids, void *decoded_request_method);
functions.description: Sends a request method and waits for one of the expected reply methods, returning a detailed amqp_rpc_reply_t describing success or server/library exceptions.
requirements: state must be valid and connected.
expected_reply_ids must be a 0-terminated array of method numbers.
decoded_request_method must point to the correct decoded request struct for request_id.
Caller must inspect reply_type and on SERVER_EXCEPTION handle CHANNEL_CLOSE or CONNECTION_CLOSE per docs; on LIBRARY_EXCEPTION inspect library_error.

functions.name: amqp_simple_rpc_decoded
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT void *AMQP_CALL amqp_simple_rpc_decoded(amqp_connection_state_t state, amqp_channel_t channel, amqp_method_number_t request_id, amqp_method_number_t reply_id, void *decoded_request_method);
functions.description: Sends a request method and waits for a specific reply method, returning a pointer to the decoded reply on success or NULL on error. Use amqp_get_rpc_reply() to obtain error details.
requirements: state must be valid and connected.
decoded_request_method must match request_id.
reply_id specifies the expected reply; mismatch leads to NULL and error in amqp_get_rpc_reply().
Returned pointer refers to library-managed memory; lifetime rules follow standard connection-buffer ownership (may be invalidated by buffer release).

functions.name: amqp_get_rpc_reply
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_rpc_reply_t AMQP_CALL amqp_get_rpc_reply(amqp_connection_state_t state);
functions.description: Returns the most recent per-connection amqp_rpc_reply_t for operations that return decoded method pointers (i.e., that return NULL on error but not amqp_rpc_reply_t).
requirements: state must be valid.
Only meaningful after an API that sets this per-connection reply state (generally APIs returning decoded pointers).

functions.name: amqp_login
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_rpc_reply_t AMQP_CALL amqp_login(amqp_connection_state_t state, char const *vhost, int channel_max, int frame_max, int heartbeat, amqp_sasl_method_enum sasl_method, ...);
functions.description: Performs AMQP connection negotiation and authenticates using the specified SASL method (PLAIN or EXTERNAL) with variadic credentials. Sets negotiated channel_max, frame_max, heartbeat.
requirements: state must be valid and associated with an open socket (amqp_socket_* + amqp_set_socket()).
vhost must point to the vhost string (e.g., "/").
channel_max: 0 means no limit; protocol max is 65535.
frame_max: min 4096; max 2^31-1; 131072 is a good default.
heartbeat: seconds between heartbeats; 0 disables.
sasl_method determines required variadic args: for AMQP_SASL_METHOD_PLAIN provide const char* username, const char* password; for AMQP_SASL_METHOD_EXTERNAL provide const char* identity.
Caller must check reply_type and handle SERVER_EXCEPTION or LIBRARY_EXCEPTION as documented (e.g., CONNECTION_CLOSED indicates failures such as invalid vhost or auth failure).

functions.name: amqp_login_with_properties
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_rpc_reply_t AMQP_CALL amqp_login_with_properties(amqp_connection_state_t state, char const *vhost, int channel_max, int frame_max, int heartbeat, const amqp_table_t *properties, amqp_sasl_method_enum sasl_method, ...);
functions.description: Like amqp_login but also sends a client properties table (commonly used for negotiating features).
requirements: Same as amqp_login() plus: properties must point to a valid amqp_table_t to send.
Variadic SASL args follow rules of amqp_login().
Caller must process amqp_rpc_reply_t as in amqp_login().

functions.name: amqp_basic_publish
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_basic_publish(amqp_connection_state_t state, amqp_channel_t channel, amqp_bytes_t exchange, amqp_bytes_t routing_key, amqp_boolean_t mandatory, amqp_boolean_t immediate, struct amqp_basic_properties_t_ const *properties, amqp_bytes_t body);
functions.description: Publishes a message (properties + body) to an exchange with a routing key. This is an async AMQP method: return value indicates transmission status, not broker-side routing/ existence errors.
requirements: state must be valid and connected; channel must be open.
exchange and routing_key are amqp_bytes_t; provide empty name for default exchange if desired.
mandatory/immediate flags are passed to broker; broker may return basic.return (not reflected in return value).
properties may be NULL or point to a valid properties struct; tables inside must fit in one frame or AMQP_STATUS_TABLE_TOO_BIG is returned.
Caller must handle amqp_status_enum errors including TIMER_FAILURE, HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT, NO_MEMORY, TABLE_TOO_BIG, CONNECTION_CLOSED, SSL/TCP errors.

functions.name: amqp_channel_close
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_rpc_reply_t AMQP_CALL amqp_channel_close(amqp_connection_state_t state, amqp_channel_t channel, int code);
functions.description: Closes the specified channel with the given reply code and returns the result.
requirements: state must be valid and connected.
channel must be a valid (possibly open) channel id.
code should be an AMQP reply code (AMQP_REPLY_SUCCESS is a good default).
Caller must inspect amqp_rpc_reply_t result.

functions.name: amqp_connection_close
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_rpc_reply_t AMQP_CALL amqp_connection_close(amqp_connection_state_t state, int code);
functions.description: Closes the entire connection, implicitly closing all channels, waits for broker acknowledgment, and closes the socket.
requirements: state must be valid and connected (or partially connected).
code is an AMQP reply code (AMQP_REPLY_SUCCESS recommended).
Caller must inspect amqp_rpc_reply_t result and stop using the connection afterwards.

functions.name: amqp_basic_ack
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_basic_ack(amqp_connection_state_t state, amqp_channel_t channel, uint64_t delivery_tag, amqp_boolean_t multiple);
functions.description: Sends a basic.ack to acknowledge one message (or multiple if multiple=1) identified by delivery_tag on a channel.
requirements: state must be valid and connected; channel open.
delivery_tag must be a valid tag previously delivered to this channel.
Return 0 indicates the ack frame was sent; negative on failure to send (does not report broker processing failures).

functions.name: amqp_basic_get
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_rpc_reply_t AMQP_CALL amqp_basic_get(amqp_connection_state_t state, amqp_channel_t channel, amqp_bytes_t queue, amqp_boolean_t no_ack);
functions.description: Synchronously performs basic.get on the given queue, retrieving one message if available.
requirements: state must be valid and connected; channel open.
queue must be a valid queue name.
If no_ack is false, caller must later ack via amqp_basic_ack; if true, broker auto-acks.
Caller must inspect amqp_rpc_reply_t for success or failure.

functions.name: amqp_basic_reject
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_basic_reject(amqp_connection_state_t state, amqp_channel_t channel, uint64_t delivery_tag, amqp_boolean_t requeue);
functions.description: Sends a basic.reject for the specified delivery_tag; optionally requeue or discard.
requirements: state must be valid and connected; channel open.
delivery_tag must be a valid tag for the channel.
Return 0 on success (frame sent); negative on failure to send. Does not indicate broker-side handling.

functions.name: amqp_basic_nack
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_basic_nack(amqp_connection_state_t state, amqp_channel_t channel, uint64_t delivery_tag, amqp_boolean_t multiple, amqp_boolean_t requeue);
functions.description: Sends a basic.nack for one or multiple unacknowledged deliveries on the channel; optionally requeue.
requirements: state must be valid and connected; channel open.
delivery_tag must be a valid tag for the channel.
multiple=1 to nack all unacked on channel; otherwise single tag.
Returns AMQP_STATUS_OK on success; otherwise negative amqp_status_enum.

functions.name: amqp_data_in_buffer
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_boolean_t AMQP_CALL amqp_data_in_buffer(amqp_connection_state_t state);
functions.description: Returns whether there is unread data remaining in the connection’s socket read buffer.
requirements: state must be valid.
TRUE implies amqp_simple_wait_frame may not block immediately.

functions.name: amqp_error_string
functions.signature: AMQP_DEPRECATED_EXPORT char *AMQP_CALL amqp_error_string(int err);
functions.description: Deprecated: Returns a heap-allocated human-readable string for the given error code. Caller must free.
requirements: err must be an amqp_status_enum (or related) error code.
Caller must free the returned char* with free().

functions.name: amqp_error_string2
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT const char *AMQP_CALL amqp_error_string2(int err);
functions.description: Returns a statically allocated string describing the given error code. No free required.
requirements: err must be an error code understood by the library.
Returned pointer must not be freed or modified.

functions.name: amqp_decode_table
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_decode_table(amqp_bytes_t encoded, amqp_pool_t *pool, amqp_table_t *output, size_t *offset);
functions.description: Deserializes a field table from AMQP wire format in encoded into output, allocating entries from pool, advancing offset.
requirements: encoded.bytes/.len must point to the serialized buffer.
pool must be an initialized amqp_pool_t for allocations.
output must be a valid pointer; existing entries will be cleared/overwritten.
offset must point to the starting position and will be updated to the end of the table.
Caller must handle AMQP_STATUS_NO_MEMORY and AMQP_STATUS_BAD_AMQP_DATA on error.

functions.name: amqp_encode_table
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_encode_table(amqp_bytes_t encoded, amqp_table_t *input, size_t *offset);
functions.description: Serializes the given field table into encoded buffer, advancing offset.
requirements: encoded.bytes/.len must have enough space to hold the serialized table; otherwise AMQP_STATUS_TABLE_TOO_BIG is returned.
input must point to a valid table to serialize.
offset must point to current write position and is updated after writing.
Caller must handle AMQP_STATUS_TABLE_TOO_BIG and AMQP_STATUS_BAD_AMQP_DATA.

functions.name: amqp_table_clone
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_table_clone(const amqp_table_t *original, amqp_table_t *clone, amqp_pool_t *pool);
functions.description: Creates a deep copy of a table into clone, allocating from pool.
requirements: original must point to a valid amqp_table_t.
clone must be a writable amqp_table_t to fill.
pool must be an initialized allocation pool.
Caller must handle AMQP_STATUS_NO_MEMORY and AMQP_STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER on error.

functions.name: amqp_read_message
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_rpc_reply_t AMQP_CALL amqp_read_message(amqp_connection_state_t state, amqp_channel_t channel, amqp_message_t *message, int flags);
functions.description: Reads a complete message (header + body) on the specified channel (typically after basic.get or receiving basic.deliver) into message.
requirements: state must be valid and connected; channel open.
message must point to an amqp_message_t; after success, caller must call amqp_destroy_message() to release internal allocations.
flags must be 0 (currently unused).
Caller must inspect amqp_rpc_reply_t for success.

functions.name: amqp_destroy_message
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT void AMQP_CALL amqp_destroy_message(amqp_message_t *message);
functions.description: Frees memory associated with an amqp_message_t previously filled by amqp_read_message().
requirements: message must be a pointer to a message initialized by amqp_read_message().
After call, properties/body memory within message is invalid.

functions.name: amqp_consume_message
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_rpc_reply_t AMQP_CALL amqp_consume_message(amqp_connection_state_t state, amqp_envelope_t *envelope, const struct timeval *timeout, int flags);
functions.description: Waits for a basic.deliver on any channel (typically after starting a consumer), reads the message into envelope, and returns. If another frame arrives first, returns LIBRARY_EXCEPTION with AMQP_STATUS_UNEXPECTED_STATE.
requirements: state must be valid and connected; consumption should have been started via amqp_basic_consume() (not in this header).
envelope must be a valid pointer; caller must later call amqp_destroy_envelope() to free internal allocations.
timeout may be NULL (block) or a valid timeval; on timeout returns LIBRARY_EXCEPTION with AMQP_STATUS_TIMEOUT.
flags must be 0 (currently unused).
If UNEXPECTED_STATE is returned, caller should call amqp_simple_wait_frame() to read and handle the frame.

functions.name: amqp_destroy_envelope
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT void AMQP_CALL amqp_destroy_envelope(amqp_envelope_t *envelope);
functions.description: Frees memory associated with an amqp_envelope_t previously filled by amqp_consume_message().
requirements: envelope must be a pointer to an envelope initialized by amqp_consume_message().
After call, contained message/fields are invalid.

functions.name: amqp_default_connection_info
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT void AMQP_CALL amqp_default_connection_info(struct amqp_connection_info *parsed);
functions.description: Initializes an amqp_connection_info struct to default values (user: guest, password: guest, host: localhost, vhost: "/", port: 5672).
requirements: parsed must be a valid pointer to amqp_connection_info.
Any previous pointers in parsed may be overwritten; caller manages lifetime of struct.

functions.name: amqp_parse_url
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_parse_url(char *url, struct amqp_connection_info *parsed);
functions.description: Parses an AMQP URI of the form amqp[s]://[user[:pass]@]host[:port]/[vhost] into parsed. Modifies the url buffer; parsed fields point into url's storage.
requirements: url must be a mutable, writable, null-terminated string buffer; function modifies it.
parsed must be a valid pointer to amqp_connection_info; its char* fields will point into url, so url must remain alive as long as those are used.
On success returns AMQP_STATUS_OK; on failure AMQP_STATUS_BAD_URL.

functions.name: amqp_socket_open
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_socket_open(amqp_socket_t *self, const char *host, int port);
functions.description: Opens a network connection on the given socket object to host:port (blocking). Use after configuring the socket and before assigning it to a connection.
requirements: self must be a socket object from amqp_tcp_socket_new()/amqp_ssl_socket_new().
host must be a valid hostname/IP; port a valid port.
Returns AMQP_STATUS_OK on success or negative amqp_status_enum on failure.

functions.name: amqp_socket_open_noblock
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_socket_open_noblock(amqp_socket_t *self, const char *host, int port, const struct timeval *timeout);
functions.description: Opens a network connection on the given socket object to host:port with a maximum timeout. If timeout is NULL, runs in blocking mode.
requirements: self must be a socket object from amqp_tcp_socket_new()/amqp_ssl_socket_new().
host must be valid; port valid.
timeout may be NULL (blocking) or a pointer to a timeval; on timeout returns a failure status.
Returns AMQP_STATUS_OK on success or negative amqp_status_enum on failure.

functions.name: amqp_socket_get_sockfd
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_socket_get_sockfd(amqp_socket_t *self);
functions.description: Returns the underlying OS socket descriptor used by the socket object, or -1 if none.
requirements: self must be a valid socket object.
Use returned descriptor cautiously; external I/O can break invariants.

functions.name: amqp_get_socket
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_socket_t *AMQP_CALL amqp_get_socket(amqp_connection_state_t state);
functions.description: Returns the amqp_socket_t associated with the connection, or NULL if none is assigned.
requirements: state must be a valid connection state.
Returned pointer is owned by the connection; do not free.

functions.name: amqp_get_server_properties
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_table_t *AMQP_CALL amqp_get_server_properties(amqp_connection_state_t state);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the broker properties table advertised on connection. Owned by the connection; read-only.
requirements: state must be valid.
Do not modify or free the returned table; lifetime is tied to the connection.

functions.name: amqp_get_client_properties
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_table_t *AMQP_CALL amqp_get_client_properties(amqp_connection_state_t state);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the client properties table that was sent to the broker on connection. Owned by the connection; read-only.
requirements: state must be valid.
Do not modify or free the returned table; lifetime is tied to the connection.

functions.name: amqp_get_handshake_timeout
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT struct timeval *AMQP_CALL amqp_get_handshake_timeout(amqp_connection_state_t state);
functions.description: Returns the current client-side login handshake timeout for the connection as a pointer to a timeval owned by the connection (NULL means infinite).
requirements: state must be valid.
Returned pointer must not be freed or modified; value may change after amqp_set_handshake_timeout().

functions.name: amqp_set_handshake_timeout
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_set_handshake_timeout(amqp_connection_state_t state, const struct timeval *timeout);
functions.description: Sets the client-side login handshake timeout used by amqp_login/amqp_login_with_properties.
requirements: state must be valid.
timeout may be NULL (infinite) or point to a valid timeval; value is copied internally and the caller retains ownership.
Must be called before amqp_login/_with_properties to change the default for login handshake.
Returns AMQP_STATUS_OK on success.

functions.name: amqp_get_rpc_timeout
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT struct timeval *AMQP_CALL amqp_get_rpc_timeout(amqp_connection_state_t state);
functions.description: Returns the current RPC timeout for the connection (NULL means infinite). Intended for advanced use; when RPCs time out, they return AMQP_STATUS_TIMEOUT and the connection is closed.
requirements: state must be valid.
Returned timeval* is owned by the connection; do not free or modify.

functions.name: amqp_set_rpc_timeout
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_set_rpc_timeout(amqp_connection_state_t state, const struct timeval *timeout);
functions.description: Sets the timeout used for RPC-style AMQP commands. Advanced feature—be aware that timed-out RPCs close the connection.
requirements: state must be valid.
timeout may be NULL (infinite) or a valid timeval pointer; value is copied internally.
Caller must handle that subsequent RPCs will time out after this interval and close the connection on timeout.
Returns AMQP_STATUS_SUCCESS (AMQP_STATUS_OK) on success.

functions.name: amqp_publisher_confirm_wait
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_rpc_reply_t AMQP_CALL amqp_publisher_confirm_wait(amqp_connection_state_t state, const struct timeval *timeout, amqp_publisher_confirm_t *result);
functions.description: Waits for a publisher confirm (ack/nack/reject) on any channel in confirm-select mode. On success, reply_type is AMQP_RESPONSE_NORMAL and result describes channel, method, and payload. On timeout, returns LIBRARY_EXCEPTION with AMQP_STATUS_TIMEOUT. If a non-ack frame is received, returns LIBRARY_EXCEPTION with AMQP_STATUS_UNEXPECTED_STATE.
requirements: state must be valid and have one or more channels in confirm-select mode.
result must be a valid pointer to receive the confirmation details.
timeout may be NULL (blocking) or a valid timeval.
Caller must inspect amqp_rpc_reply_t: on NORMAL, use result->method to select the union member in result->payload; on LIBRARY_EXCEPTION, check library_error for TIMEOUT or UNEXPECTED_STATE.

functions.name: amqp_constant_name
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT char const *AMQP_CALL amqp_constant_name(int constantNumber);
functions.description: Returns a human-readable name for an AMQP constant (status/condition code). The returned string is owned by the library and must not be freed by the caller.
requirements: Input constantNumber may be any integer AMQP constant value.
The returned pointer is to memory managed by the library; the caller must not free() it.
Thread-safety and lifetime of the returned pointer beyond immediate use are unknown (not documented).

functions.name: amqp_constant_is_hard_error
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_boolean_t AMQP_CALL amqp_constant_is_hard_error(int constantNumber);
functions.description: Determines whether an AMQP constant represents a hard error that requires closing the connection.
requirements: Input constantNumber may be any integer AMQP constant value.
Returns a boolean-like amqp_boolean_t (0 = false, non-zero = true).

functions.name: amqp_method_name
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT char const *AMQP_CALL amqp_method_name(amqp_method_number_t methodNumber);
functions.description: Returns a human-readable name for an AMQP method number. The returned string is owned by the library and must not be freed by the caller.
requirements: methodNumber must be a valid AMQP method number to obtain a meaningful name; other values may return an implementation-defined string.
The returned pointer is to memory managed by the library; the caller must not free() it.
Thread-safety and lifetime of the returned pointer beyond immediate use are unknown (not documented).

functions.name: amqp_method_has_content
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT amqp_boolean_t AMQP_CALL amqp_method_has_content(amqp_method_number_t methodNumber);
functions.description: Returns whether the given AMQP method carries content (i.e., will be followed by a properties frame and one or more body frames).
requirements: methodNumber should be an AMQP method number; non-method values yield unspecified results.
Returns a boolean-like amqp_boolean_t (0 = false, non-zero = true).

functions.name: amqp_decode_method
functions.signature: AMQP_EXPORT int AMQP_CALL amqp_decode_method(amqp_method_number_t methodNumber, amqp_pool_t *pool, amqp_bytes_t encoded, void **decoded);
functions.description: Decodes a method frame payload from AMQP wire format into a method structure allocated from the provided memory pool.
requirements: methodNumber must correspond to the type of method contained in the encoded bytes.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets inputs for:
# - amqp_cstring_bytes: expects a valid null-terminated C string (we supply bytes for FUZZ_PARAM_STR)
# - amqp_table_entry_cmp: uses keys via amqp_cstring_bytes with max 128 bytes (<=127 chars before NUL)
# The fuzz harness will take our bytes and produce std::string values for FUZZ_PARAM_STR, which are
# then passed to amqp_cstring_bytes(k.c_str()). Our job is to provide interesting, but valid, string
# contents that exercise comparisons and typical AMQP key/mechanism/content strings.
#
# Design goals:
# - Mix of ASCII, UTF-8, and edge-case strings (empty, max-length 127, differing prefixes/suffixes)
# - Include characters relevant to AMQP names (letters, digits, '.', '-', '_', ':', '/', '*', '#')
# - Include varying cases for ordering differences
# - Include embedded spaces and punctuation
# - Ensure strings are valid as std::string data and suitable for c_str() (std::string manages NUL)
# Note: We avoid embedded NUL since FUZZ_PARAM_STR uses std::string and typical table keys are
# documented as null-terminated strings; embedded NUL would truncate at first NUL when wrapped.

AMQP_NAME_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + ".-_:/*#"  # typical AMQP routing/key charset
PRINTABLE_EXTRA = " !?$@[]{}(),;+'\"\\|<>~`^%&="
UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "προβάτον",              # Greek
    "こんにちは",            # Japanese
    "зайчик",                # Cyrillic
    "emoji-🙂🙃🚀",          # Emoji
    "हिंदी-परीक्षण",        # Hindi
    "中文測試",               # CJK
]

COMMON_AMQP_KEYS = [
    "content-type",
    "content_encoding",
    "headers",
    "delivery_mode",
    "priority",
    "correlation_id",
    "reply_to",
    "expiration",
    "message_id",
    "timestamp",
    "type",
    "user_id",
    "app_id",
    "cluster_id",
    "x-match",
    "alternate-exchange",
    "dead-letter-exchange",
    "dead-letter-routing-key",
]

ROUTING_KEYS = [
    "",
    "#",
    "*",
    "foo",
    "foo.bar",
    "foo.*.bar",
    "a.b.c",
    "orders.created",
    "orders.*",
    "*.critical",
]

EXCHANGES = ["", "amq.direct", "amq.topic", "amq.fanout", "amq.headers", "logs", "events"]
QUEUES = ["", "task_queue", "rpc_queue", "retry-queue", "dead-letter-queue", "durable_q"]

# Helper to create a random AMQP-like name of up to 127 chars

def rand_name(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 0, max_len: int = 127) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(AMQP_NAME_CHARS) for _ in range(n))

# Helper to create a printable mixed string

def rand_printable(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 127) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    alphabet = AMQP_NAME_CHARS + PRINTABLE_EXTRA
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

# Construct pairs that will be compared: encourage different ordering outcomes

def build_interesting_pairs(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    candidates: List[str] = []

    # Edge cases
    candidates.append("")  # empty
    candidates.append("a")
    candidates.append("A")
    candidates.append("0")

    # Max length boundary (127)
    candidates.append("a" * 127)
    candidates.append("Z" * 127)

    # Different prefixes/suffixes
    candidates.append("abc")
    candidates.append("abcd")  # longer suffix
    candidates.append("abC")    # case diff

    # Names and keys
    candidates.extend(COMMON_AMQP_KEYS)
    candidates.extend(rng.sample(ROUTING_KEYS, k=len(ROUTING_KEYS)))
    candidates.extend(rng.sample(EXCHANGES, k=len(EXCHANGES)))
    candidates.extend(rng.sample(QUEUES, k=len(QUEUES)))

    # Random names
    for _ in range(6):
        candidates.append(rand_name(rng, 1, rng.choice([5, 16, 32, 64, 100, 127])))

    # Printable with punctuation
    for _ in range(4):
        candidates.append(rand_printable(rng, rng.choice([10, 20, 40, 80, 120])))

    # Some Unicode strings (UTF-8)
    candidates.extend(rng.sample(UNICODE_SAMPLES, k=min(3, len(UNICODE_SAMPLES))))

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq: List[str] = []
    for s in candidates:
        if s not in seen and len(s) <= 127:
            seen.add(s)
            uniq.append(s)
    return uniq

# Compose final buffer: concatenate multiple strings separated by newlines.
# The fuzzer harness will usually request multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() independently,
# but when a single buffer seeds a corpus, providing many lines increases variety.


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    lines: List[str] = []

    # Build a pool of interesting strings
    pool = build_interesting_pairs(rng)

    # Ensure presence of typical AMQP credential-like and URL-like tokens
    user = rand_name(rng, 1, 12).lower()
    password = rand_printable(rng, 16)
    host = rand_name(rng, 3, 20).lower()
    vhost = rng.choice(["/", rand_name(rng, 1, 10)])
    port = rng.choice([5672, 5671, 5673, rng.randint(1000, 65535)])

    amqp_url = f"amqp://{user}:{password}@{host}:{port}/{vhost}"
    lines.append(amqp_url)

    # Mechanisms/locales/examples (used in start/start-ok fields commonly)
    lines.append("PLAIN")
    lines.append("EXTERNAL")
    lines.append("en_US")
    lines.append("en_US.UTF-8")

    # Include exchanges, queues, routing keys explicitly
    lines.extend(EXCHANGES)
    lines.extend(QUEUES)
    lines.extend(ROUTING_KEYS)

    # Include property keys and some header-like values
    lines.extend(COMMON_AMQP_KEYS)
    lines.extend([
        "application/json",
        "text/plain",
        "gzip",
        "deflate",
        "correlation-123",
        "reply.queue",
        "60000",  # expiration millis
        "msg-" + rand_name(rng, 4, 12),
    ])

    # Add the pool
    lines.extend(pool)

    # Add a few randomized max-length strings near 127 to exercise boundary
    for _ in range(3):
        L = rng.choice([125, 126, 127])
        lines.append(rand_printable(rng, L))

    # Ensure overall size <= 4096 bytes
    out_lines: List[str] = []
    total = 0
    for s in lines:
        # Avoid embedded NULs; sanitize by removing them (unlikely here)
        if "\x00" in s:
            s = s.replace("\x00", "")
        b = s.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")
        if total + len(b) + 1 > 4096:  # +1 for newline
            break
        out_lines.append(s)
        total += len(b) + 1

    # Join with newlines so the harness can split or use whole lines as seeds
    data = ("\n".join(out_lines) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
    return data

import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# AMQP 0-9-1 wire-level helpers for building valid frames
# Frame format:
#  octet type (1)
#  short channel (2, big-endian)
#  long size (4, big-endian) = payload size
#  payload (size bytes)
#  octet frame-end = 0xCE
# Types: 1=METHOD, 2=HEADER, 3=BODY, 8=HEARTBEAT
# Header (properties) payload starts with: short class-id, short weight (0), long long body size, then property flags/values.

FRAME_END = 0xCE
FT_METHOD = 1
FT_HEADER = 2
FT_BODY = 3
FT_HEARTBEAT = 8

# Selected method numbers (class<<16 | method)
# Connection.start, connection.tune, channel.open-ok, basic.deliver, basic.ack etc.
MN_CONNECTION_START = (10 << 16) | 10
MN_CONNECTION_TUNE = (10 << 16) | 30
MN_CHANNEL_OPEN_OK = (20 << 16) | 11
MN_BASIC_DELIVER = (60 << 16) | 60
MN_BASIC_ACK = (60 << 16) | 80
MN_BASIC_RETURN = (60 << 16) | 50

# Class IDs
CLASS_CONNECTION = 10
CLASS_CHANNEL = 20
CLASS_BASIC = 60

# Property flags bits for basic properties (from high to low). We will just set a couple safely
PROP_CONTENT_TYPE = 1 << (15 - 0)  # first bit in 16-bit field
PROP_DELIVERY_MODE = 1 << (15 - 3)

# Helpers to encode AMQP shortstr and longstr per spec
# shortstr: 1-byte length, then UTF-8 bytes (length must fit in 255)
# longstr: 4-byte length, then bytes

def enc_shortstr(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    if len(s) > 255:
        s = s[:255]
    return struct.pack('!B', len(s)) + s


def enc_longstr(b: bytes) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('!I', len(b)) + b


def frame(type_octet: int, channel: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('!BHI', type_octet, channel, len(payload)) + payload + struct.pack('!B', FRAME_END)


# Build some common valid method payloads with simple fields

def m_connection_start_payload() -> bytes:
    # connection.start: version-major (octet), version-minor (octet), server-properties (table), mechanisms (longstr), locales (longstr)
    # We keep server-properties as empty table: 4-byte length then no entries
    server_props = struct.pack('!I', 0)
    mechanisms = enc_longstr(b"PLAIN")
    locales = enc_longstr(b"en_US")
    return struct.pack('!BB', 0, 9) + server_props + mechanisms + locales


def m_connection_tune_payload(frame_max: int = 131072, heartbeat: int = 0) -> bytes:
    # channel-max (short), frame-max (long), heartbeat (short)
    return struct.pack('!H I H', 0, frame_max, heartbeat)


def m_channel_open_ok_payload() -> bytes:
    # channel.open-ok: shortstr channel-id (arbitrary)
    return enc_shortstr(b"ch-1")


def m_basic_deliver_payload(routing_key: bytes = b"rk") -> bytes:
    # consumer-tag (shortstr), delivery-tag (longlong), redelivered (bit in octet), exchange (shortstr), routing-key (shortstr)
    return b"".join([
        enc_shortstr(b"ctag"),
        struct.pack('!Q', 1),
        struct.pack('!B', 0),
        enc_shortstr(b"ex"),
        enc_shortstr(routing_key),
    ])


def m_basic_ack_payload(multiple: bool = False) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('!Q B', 1, 1 if multiple else 0)


def m_basic_return_payload() -> bytes:
    # reply-code (short), reply-text (shortstr), exchange (shortstr), routing-key (shortstr)
    return struct.pack('!H', 312) + enc_shortstr(b"NO_ROUTE") + enc_shortstr(b"ex") + enc_shortstr(b"rk")


def method_frame(method_number: int, channel: int, args_payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # payload: class-id (short), method-id (short), then args
    class_id = (method_number >> 16) & 0xFFFF
    method_id = method_number & 0xFFFF
    payload = struct.pack('!HH', class_id, method_id) + args_payload
    return frame(FT_METHOD, channel, payload)


# Build a properties (HEADER) frame for basic class with a small body size and minimal properties set

def header_frame_basic(channel: int, body_size: int, with_props: bool = True) -> bytes:
    # class-id (short), weight (short=0), body size (long long), property flags (short[, short...]), then values
    base = struct.pack('!HHQ', CLASS_BASIC, 0, body_size)
    if with_props:
        flags = 0
        values = b""
        # content-type as shortstr
        flags |= PROP_CONTENT_TYPE
        values += enc_shortstr(b"text/plain")
        # delivery-mode as octet
        flags |= PROP_DELIVERY_MODE
        values += struct.pack('!B', 2)
        payload = base + struct.pack('!H', flags) + values
    else:
        payload = base + struct.pack('!H', 0)
    return frame(FT_HEADER, channel, payload)


def body_frame(channel: int, chunk: bytes) -> bytes:
    return frame(FT_BODY, channel, chunk)


def heartbeat_frame() -> bytes:
    return frame(FT_HEARTBEAT, 0, b"")


def build_scenarios(rnd: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    scenarios: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) A lone heartbeat frame
    scenarios.append(heartbeat_frame())

    # 2) A simple method frame: connection.start
    scenarios.append(method_frame(MN_CONNECTION_START, channel=0, args_payload=m_connection_start_payload()))

    # 3) connection.tune method
    fm = rnd.choice([4096, 8192, 65535, 131072, 262144])
    hb = rnd.choice([0, 1, 5, 60])
    scenarios.append(method_frame(MN_CONNECTION_TUNE, 0, m_connection_tune_payload(fm, hb)))

    # 4) channel.open-ok on channel 1
    scenarios.append(method_frame(MN_CHANNEL_OPEN_OK, 1, m_channel_open_ok_payload()))

    # 5) A proper content triplet: basic.deliver + header + body (possibly split bodies)
    body_variants = [b"hello", b"", b"x" * rnd.randint(1, 64), b"JSON:{\"k\":\"v\"}"]
    body = rnd.choice(body_variants)
    ch = rnd.randint(1, 4)
    scenarios.append(method_frame(MN_BASIC_DELIVER, ch, m_basic_deliver_payload()))
    scenarios.append(header_frame_basic(ch, len(body), with_props=True))
    if len(body) <= 16 or rnd.random() < 0.5:
        scenarios.append(body_frame(ch, body))
    else:
        # split body into a few chunks
        pos = 0
        while pos < len(body):
            n = rnd.randint(1, min(16, len(body) - pos))
            scenarios.append(body_frame(ch, body[pos:pos + n]))
            pos += n

    # 6) basic.ack method on another channel
    scenarios.append(method_frame(MN_BASIC_ACK, rnd.randint(1, 4), m_basic_ack_payload(multiple=rnd.choice([False, True]))))

    # 7) basic.return (undeliverable publish)
    scenarios.append(method_frame(MN_BASIC_RETURN, rnd.randint(1, 4), m_basic_return_payload()))

    # 8) Mix multiple frames together to simulate buffered stream
    # Choose 2-4 random earlier frames and concatenate
    mix = b"".join(rnd.choice(scenarios) for _ in range(rnd.randint(2, 4)))
    scenarios.append(mix)

    return scenarios


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    scenarios = build_scenarios(rnd)

    # Choose one or concatenate a few to form up to 512 bytes (fuzzer caps to 512)
    choice = rnd.choice(["one", "concat"])
    if choice == "one":
        buf = rnd.choice(scenarios)
    else:
        buf = b""
        rnd.shuffle(scenarios)
        for s in scenarios:
            if len(buf) + len(s) > 512:
                break
            buf += s
    # Ensure non-empty and within limit
    if not buf:
        buf = heartbeat_frame()
    return buf[:512]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for AMQP URL strings suitable for amqp_parse_url.
# The fuzzer stub ensures the buffer is mutable and null-terminated, and prefixes
# amqp:// if missing. Our job is to provide already interesting but valid URLs.
# We keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

SCHEMES = ["amqp", "amqps"]
HOSTS = [
    "localhost",
    "127.0.0.1",
    "::1",
    "example.com",
    "broker.internal",
    "xn--exmple-cua.com",  # punycode-ish
]
VHOSTS = ["/", "%2F", "vhost", "prod", "staging", "a/b", "v%2Fhost", "~user", "☕"]
USERS = ["guest", "user", "admin", "u", "test", "service-account", "user.name"]
PASS_FRAGMENTS = ["guest", "p@ss", "secret", "", "1234", "with:colon", "a:b:c", "slash/inside", "sp ace", "ümlaut"]
ROLES = ["", "?heartbeat=0", "?heartbeat=10", "?frame_max=131072", "?channel_max=0", "?frame_max=4096&heartbeat=5"]

SAFE_UNRESERVED = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-._~"


def percent_encode(s: str) -> str:
    out = []
    for ch in s:
        if ch in SAFE_UNRESERVED:
            out.append(ch)
        else:
            out.append('%{:02X}'.format(ord(ch)))
    return ''.join(out)


def maybe(s: str, prob: float, alt: str) -> str:
    return s if random.random() < prob else alt


def rand_port() -> int:
    # Include edge and typical values
    return random.choice([0, 1, 80, 443, 25672, 5671, 5672, 65535, random.randint(2, 65534)])


def rand_userinfo() -> str:
    # user[:pass] with percent-encoding variations
    user = random.choice(USERS)
    # Sometimes include special characters to exercise parser and percent-encoding
    if random.random() < 0.4:
        user += random.choice(["", ".", "-", "_", "+"]) + ''.join(random.choice("._-") for _ in range(random.randint(0, 2)))
    if random.random() < 0.3:
        user = percent_encode(user)

    include_pass = random.random() < 0.8
    if not include_pass:
        return user
    pw = random.choice(PASS_FRAGMENTS)
    if random.random() < 0.5:
        # sprinkle additional characters
        pw += random.choice(["", "!", "@", ":", "/", "?"])
    if random.random() < 0.5:
        pw = percent_encode(pw)
    return f"{user}:{pw}"


def rand_host() -> str:
    kind = random.random()
    if kind < 0.6:
        return random.choice(HOSTS)
    elif kind < 0.8:
        # IPv6 literal in brackets
        hextets = [format(random.randint(0, 0xFFFF), 'x') for _ in range(8)]
        return f"[{'::' if random.random()<0.3 else ':'.join(hextets)}]"
    else:
        # domain with labels and digits
        labels = []
        for _ in range(random.randint(2, 4)):
            lablen = random.randint(1, 10)
            label = random.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) + ''.join(random.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + '-') for _ in range(lablen-1))
            labels.append(label.strip('-') or 'a')
        return '.'.join(labels)


def rand_vhost() -> str:
    v = random.choice(VHOSTS)
    # Sometimes build path-like vhosts; amqp URI uses path component after '/'
    if random.random() < 0.4:
        segs: List[str] = []
        for _ in range(random.randint(1, 3)):
            seg = ''.join(random.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ .:") for _ in range(random.randint(1, 6)))
            if random.random() < 0.4:
                seg = percent_encode(seg)
            segs.append(seg)
        v = '/'.join(segs)
    # Ensure leading slash semantics in URI: we will add '/' before vhost
    return v


def build_url() -> str:
    scheme = random.choice(SCHEMES)
    # userinfo@
    userinfo = rand_userinfo() if random.random() < 0.9 else ""
    userinfo_part = (userinfo + '@') if userinfo else ""

    host = rand_host()
    # optional :port
    port = rand_port()
    port_part = f":{port}" if random.random() < 0.8 else ""

    # optional vhost after '/'
    vhost = rand_vhost() if random.random() < 0.95 else ""
    # For AMQP URLs, an empty path means '/' vhost; sometimes use empty intentionally
    path_part = "/" + vhost if (vhost != "") or (random.random() < 0.7) else ""

    # Optional query params (non-standard but tolerated by some parsers)
    query = random.choice(ROLES) if random.random() < 0.3 else ""

    url = f"{scheme}://{userinfo_part}{host}{port_part}{path_part}{query}"
    # Keep within 512 range expected by stub; but generator size limit is 4096 anyway
    return url[:512]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    random.seed(seed)
    # Build multiple URL variants and pick one to add variety based on seed
    variants = []
    for _ in range(4):
        variants.append(build_url())
    # Also include minimal and edge-case forms explicitly
    variants.append("amqp://localhost")
    variants.append("amqp://guest:guest@localhost/")
    variants.append("amqps://user:pass@example.com:5671/%2F")
    variants.append("amqp://[::1]:5672/")
    # Choose one deterministically from seed but with some randomness
    choice = variants[seed % len(variants)]
    return choice.encode('utf-8')
